text: The Protection of Plant Varieties and Farmers' Rights Act 2001 (PPVFR) provides IP protection for new plant varieties. Administered by PPV&FR Authority. Protects: varieties of specified crops (109+ species including medicinal/aromatic plants). Registration grants exclusive rights to produce, sell, market, distribute, import, export the variety. Duration: 15 years (18 for trees/vines) from registration. For AYUSH: cultivated medicinal plants (Ashwagandha, Tulsi, Brahmi, Shatavari) can be protected if new varieties developed through breeding.

Requirements for registration under PPVFR: 1) NOVELTY — variety not commercially exploited in India for >1 year (4 years outside India) before filing. 2) DISTINCTIVENESS — clearly distinguishable from other known varieties by at least one characteristic. 3) UNIFORMITY — subject to variation expected from propagation, variety is sufficiently uniform. 4) STABILITY — relevant characteristics remain unchanged after repeated propagation. Categories: New variety, Extant variety (existing but not registered), Farmers' variety (developed by farming communities). For AYUSH: new high-yield or high-alkaloid varieties of medicinal plants qualify.

PVP registration process: 1) File application with PPV&FR Authority. 2) Pay fees (Rs 2,000-50,000 based on variety type). 3) Application published in Plant Variety Journal. 4) Opposition period (3 months from publication). 5) DUS testing (Distinctness, Uniformity, Stability) — conducted at designated centers. 6) Examination and decision. 7) Registration certificate issued. 8) Variety entered in National Register. Timeline: 2-4 years including DUS testing. Maintain material for DUS at designated gene bank.

Registered variety grants breeder exclusive rights to: 1) Produce, sell, market, distribute the variety. 2) Determine authorization for others to do above. 3) Exclusive right to protected propagating material. Rights don't extend to: acts done privately for non-commercial purposes, experimental/research use, use as source for creating other varieties (breeders' exemption — key difference from patents). For AYUSH: develop new varieties of medicinal plants through conventional breeding or modern techniques, register for PVP protection.

Unique feature of Indian PPVFR — extensive farmers' rights: Section 39: Farmers can save, use, sow, resow, exchange, share, sell their farm produce INCLUDING from protected varieties (but not sell as 'branded seed' of protected variety). Section 41: Farmers entitled to rewards for contribution to varieties. Section 42: Farmers' varieties can be registered by communities. Section 44: Communities entitled to benefit-sharing for use of community varieties. For AYUSH: sourcing from farmer-cultivated medicinal plants involves these rights — respect farmers' ability to save and share seeds.

Essentially Derived Variety (EDV): derived from initial variety, retaining essential characteristics. Example: mutant of protected variety. EDV can be registered but requires authorization from original variety holder for commercialization. Prevents minor modifications creating new variety rights that circumvent original protection. For AYUSH: if you mutate or minimally modify someone's protected medicinal plant variety, it may be EDV requiring their permission.

Benefit sharing under PPVFR: 1) If registered variety developed using genetic material from India, Authority can require benefit sharing with communities. 2) National Gene Fund receives fees from variety registration. 3) Farmers/communities contributing to variety development entitled to rewards from Gene Fund. 4) Benefit sharing claims can be filed by communities against registered varieties. For AYUSH: if variety uses germplasm from specific region/community, benefit sharing may apply — document sourcing and community engagement.

Comparison for AYUSH: PVP (PPVFR Act) — protects plant varieties as such, allows farmers' and breeders' exemptions, 15-18 year term, relatively cheaper. PATENT (Patents Act) — protects processes for plant development (genetic modification), no farmers' exemption, 20 year term, more expensive and difficult. Key: in India, plants/seeds themselves cannot be patented (Section 3(j)), only processes. Use PVP for varietal protection, patents for genetic modification processes. Both can apply to same innovation.

Medicinal plants in PPV&FR notification: Ashwagandha (Withania somnifera), Tulsi (Ocimum sanctum), Senna (Cassia angustifolia), Isabgol (Plantago ovata), Safed Musli (Chlorophytum borivilianum), Kalmegh (Andrographis paniculata), Brahmi (Bacopa monnieri), Shatavari (Asparagus racemosus), and more. Breeding targets: higher alkaloid content, better yield, disease resistance, climate adaptation. For AYUSH raw material suppliers: develop improved varieties, register, license to growers. Creates differentiated, quality raw material supply.

DUS (Distinctness, Uniformity, Stability) testing validates variety characteristics: 1) Grow variety alongside reference varieties. 2) Observe morphological characteristics per crop-specific descriptors. 3) At least 2 growth cycles for annuals, longer for perennials. 4) Centers: designated institutions (ICAR, SAUs, private recognized centers). 5) Applicant provides propagating material. 6) Authority bears testing cost (included in fees). For AYUSH medicinal plants: DUS descriptors include phytochemical characteristics (alkaloid content) where available.

PVP infringement: unauthorized use of protected variety's propagating material. Remedies: injunction, damages, seizure. Criminal penalties: imprisonment up to 3 years and/or fine up to Rs 20 lakh. Note: innocent infringer defense available (didn't know of registration). Inspection: Plant Variety Protection Authorities can appoint inspectors. For AYUSH: if you develop a registered high-alkaloid variety, can prevent competitors from selling seeds of that variety. Enforcement practically challenging for plants that look similar.

International systems: UPOV (International Union for Protection of New Varieties of Plants) — India is NOT a member. India's PPVFR is 'sui generis' system with stronger farmers' rights than UPOV. Implication: protection in India doesn't automatically extend internationally. For international protection: file in each target country separately. UPOV member countries have mutual recognition among themselves (India excluded). For AYUSH exporters: if selling protected variety seeds internationally, secure protection in target markets.
